chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Abu Al-Abbas Al-Fadl ibn Abdul Malik, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The supplication is answered in four places: in Al-Witr, and after Al-Fajr, and after Al-Zuhr, and after Al-Maghrib.'

key_terms.يُسْتَجَابُ: is answered (passive verb referring to du'a)

ai.seo_question: What are the four times when supplications are most likely to be answered according to Imam Al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies four specific times when supplications (du'a) are particularly likely to be answered: during the Witr prayer, and after the Fajr, Dhuhr, and Maghrib prayers. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on the 'times of acceptance' (awqat al-istijabah), linking daily ritual structure with moments of heightened spiritual receptivity to divine grace.
